policy.scope: R138 bounded Oracle direction screen; no router acceptance
policy.decision: All primary conditions must pass on both pairs and no latency veto may fire. Otherwise stop this direction. No automatic extra samples or candidate variants.
policy.diagnostic_requirement: After timing, verify one fewer sendmsg per silent REMOVE and disclose user instructions per registration cycle; no mandatory instruction reduction threshold. Diagnostic timing is excluded.

mechanism.scope: post-timing diagnostics; diagnostic latency and CPU excluded from the screen

records.attribution: A successful recvmsg request prefix starts its phase. EAGAIN probes and epoll waits are assigned to the previously received request until the next successful request recvmsg. Startup precedes successful accept; connection setup, preflight, warmup, validation LOOKUPs and EOF teardown are separate from measured cycles. This is a prior-request convention, not a synchronized timed interval: the wait leading into the first measured request belongs to the prior warmup request, and the wait leading into the final LOOKUP belongs to the last measured request. epoll_wait and epoll_pwait are counted separately as printed by strace. Totals cover selected syscall families only, not every daemon syscall.

decision: Reject this direction under the frozen Oracle eligibility rule. Keep R136 unchanged; no router job or extra candidate/run.
limitations: CPU pairs are reported separately; concurrent workers share host caches and scheduler resources.
Each subject keeps one daemon for all lanes and affinity conditions within a block.
Absolute paired median <= 1% is unresolved; larger changes are descriptive directions only.
Register and event lanes use real socket protocol but Oracle rankings do not predict router acceptance.
All raw latency samples, CPU snapshots, subject results, and failed executions remain archived.
The archive verifies recorded identities; live ELF/library hashing is asserted by the runner and is not independently repeated by this offline report.
Guarded REMOVE intentionally falls back for the three named object-event lanes.
User-mode instructions exclude kernel execution; PMU hardware cycles are not registration cycles.
Oracle daemon CPU savings and confirmed syscall reduction did not resolve the primary end-to-end mean difference.
No latency veto fired; this does not establish equivalence or absence of regressions.
The rejected Oracle screen cannot establish that a router gain is impossible or that a language limit has been reached.
